newsitem.title: CHINA: Spain's Santander official happy with Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Santander official happy with Q1 results.

text.p: The chairman of Spain's largest bank, Banco Santander, said on Monday that he was very happy with Santander Group's results for the first quarter of 1997.

"We are very happy with the results we have attained in the first quarter," chairman Emilio Botin told reporters at a media conference organized to mark the opening of the bank's Shanghai representative office.
Santander Group will announce first quarter results in Spain on April 29, he said.
"It will be a good year for the Santander Group," Botin said.
The group, headed by Banco Santander, is engaged in retail, corporate and investment banking.
"We expect we will have 20 percent more (net) profit in 1997 than 1996," he said, adding the group registered net profit of close to $900 million in 1996.
"We expect to increase our dividend by at least 15 percent," he added.
Some 35 percent of the group's 1996 profits were made outside of Spain, and Santander would like to increase this figure to 50 percent with 10 percent of the total from Asia alone, Botin said.
Banco Santander on Monday became the first Spanish bank to establish a representative office in Shanghai, following the opening of an office in Beijing in 1993.
The bank hopes to help advise China on its reform of state enterprises, using experience gained from participating in mergers and acquisitions of companies in South America.

Santander Investment Asia, the group's investment banking arm based in Hong Kong, was chosen last week to act as a financial adviser for two liquefied petroleum gas projects worth $2.26 billion in eastern China.
Joseph Lai, managing director of Santander Group Hong Kong, declined to give details, but said the projects involved a large, Shanghai-based petrochemical firm.
